native_result.query: What proportion of studies in Experimental Economics were conducted in a lab setting?
native_result.HypoA: In Experimental Economics, all studies (both original and replication) were conducted in a lab setting (100%), while in Psychology, a small proportion of replication studies were also conducted online (8.8%)
native_result.HypoB: All of the studies in Experimental Economics were conducted in a lab setting — the proportion is 100% (18 out of 18). The dataset contains 18 Experimental Economics studies (project == 'ee'), each with online.o = 0 (the original experiment was not conducted online), which given the schema is the only defensible indicator of a lab setting. This is corroborated by the subject profile (17 student samples and 1 community sample, none marked as 'online' subjects) and by the fact that the replications were also run in labs (online.r = 0 for all 18), so the answer is robust to either interpretation of "studies".
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv (927 rows). Filtered to project == 'ee': 18 rows, 18 unique ids (ee.1–ee.18), one row per study (lab_id all NaN, drop all False — no deduplication needed). Defined lab setting as online flag == 0 (online.o for original studies), the only setting indicator in the schema; us_lab.o was treated as a US-location flag, not a lab/online flag. Computed online.o value counts and missing counts: 0.0 × 18, 0 missing → 18/18 = 100% of original EE studies were lab-based. Robustness check on replications (online.r): 0.0 × 18, 0 missing → also 100%, so the answer holds under either interpretation. Sanity-checked the row count against the second CSV, which has exactly 18 rows labeled 'Experimental Economics', matching the EE subset.
